# Judith Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** In the eighteenth year, on the twenty-second day of the first month, a decree went forth from the house of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians to take vengeance on all the land, just as he had declared.

**2:2** He called together all his servants and all his nobles and laid before them his secret plan, detailing with his own mouth every evil purpose against every land.

**2:3** They decided to destroy all who had not obeyed the word of his mouth.

**2:4** When he had finished setting out his plan, Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians summoned Holofernes, the chief commander of his army, who was second only to himself, and said to him:

**2:5** "Thus says the great king, the lord of all the earth: Go forth from my presence and take with you men confident in their own strength — one hundred and twenty thousand infantry and twelve thousand mounted archers —

**2:6** and march out against all the western lands, because they have disobeyed the command of my mouth.

**2:7** Order them to have earth and water ready, for I am coming out against them in my anger. I will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of my army and give them over as plunder.

**2:8** Their slain shall fill every ravine and gully; the river will be choked with their dead; and every overflowing stream and mountain valley will be filled with the corpses of their flesh.

**2:9** I will lead their captives to the ends of all the earth.

**2:10** But you — go and occupy all their territory in advance. If they surrender to you, hold them for me until the day of their punishment.

**2:11** As for those who resist, show no pity — give them over to slaughter and plunder throughout all your land.

**2:12** For as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, I have spoken, and I will accomplish this by my own hand.

**2:13** As for you — do not violate any of the commands of your lord, but carry them out exactly as I have commanded you, and do not delay in doing them."

**2:14** Then Holofernes went out from before his lord and summoned all the commanders and generals and officers of the Assyrian army.

**2:15** He mustered chosen men for battle as his lord had commanded — one hundred and twenty thousand infantry and twelve thousand mounted archers —

**2:16** and arranged them as a great host is arranged for war.

**2:17** He took camels and donkeys and mules in very great numbers for their baggage train, and sheep and oxen and goats without number for their provisions.

**2:18** Every man was fully supplied with provisions, and there was a great amount of gold and silver from the royal treasury.

**2:19** Then he set out — he and his entire force — to march ahead of King Nebuchadnezzar, covering all the face of the western region with their chariots and cavalry and chosen infantry.

**2:20** A mixed multitude like locusts and like the sand of the earth went along with them, beyond all counting.

**2:21** They marched out from Nineveh three days' journey toward the plain of Bectileth and encamped near Bectileth beside the mountain that lies to the left of Upper Cilicia.

**2:22** From there he took his whole army — infantry, cavalry, and chariots — and led them into the hill country.

**2:23** He ravaged Phud and Lud, plundered all the Rassites and the Ishmaelites who lived along the edge of the desert, south of the land of the Chellaeans.

**2:24** He crossed the Euphrates and passed through Mesopotamia, demolishing every fortified city along the brook Abron all the way to the sea.

**2:25** He seized the territory of Cilicia, cut down all who opposed him, and advanced to the borders of Japheth, which faced southward toward Arabia.

**2:26** He encircled all the Midianites, burned their tents, and plundered their sheepfolds.

**2:27** He swept down into the plain of Damascus during the wheat harvest, burned all their fields, destroyed their flocks and herds, plundered their cities, ravaged their plains, and put all their young men to the sword.

**2:28** Fear of him and dread of him fell upon all who lived along the seacoast — those of Sidon and Tyre, those dwelling in Sur and Okina, and all who lived in Jamnia — and those inhabiting Azotus and Ascalon were greatly afraid.
